subject: unamentis-ios
verdict: B- (persona's own grade). Scored 16/24. Nineteen minutes to a correctly ordered investigation plan, one step of which rests on code the app never runs.

orientation.note: Correct one-paragraph description at t+1m, one click from cold start. The persona later re-checked that paragraph against everything it found and reported it accurate in every particular tested.

model_accuracy.evidence: FINDINGS.md section 3, Q1 to Q5, graded against ANSWER-KEY-unamentis-ios.md P1.1 to P1.5
model_accuracy.note: Q1 correct: purpose, audience, and every moving part the key requires, including Core Data, the four protocols, the discovery ladder, on-device models and the test harnesses. Q2 partial: direct-to-provider HTTPS and WSS is right; self-hosted STT over WebSocket is right for GLM-ASR; but the management server is described as HTTPS with no port where the key has plain HTTP on hardcoded 8766 with no auth token, and the persona was blunt that the tool could not give it a port (O11). Q3 partial: the look-list is well ordered and steps 1, 3, 4 and 5 are sound; step 2, the leading hypothesis, is FallbackLLMService, which the key shows is never constructed by the app, and the key's first-order fact (no mid-session error surface at all, SessionView.swift:1457-1833) was not reached. Q4 correct: Core Data with 13 entities, Keychain, on-device model files, in-memory context, and a provider list that reconciled the Support lens's five with the tours' additional names; the LiveKit-unreferenced lead is confirmed by the key. Q5 correct: shape right, blanks stated as blanks, and the persona named the backend as the thing it could not draw.

navigation_efficiency.note: Reached every named target. Lost time to the name-only search, to the Structure lens at System and Domain levels, and to abandoning the New interface for the Classic workbench, where the persona says every useful thing it learned came from.

trust.evidence: FINDINGS.md section 5; evidence/36 (Rules), 28 (Capability), 23 (Auth concern), 20 vs 40 (Security vs Keychain), 19 (Data lens writers), 21 vs 10 (external reliance), 39 (management server)
trust.note: Two verified high incidents (Rules lens, Capability lens), two verified medium-high (Auth concern keyword noise, Security lens zero), the incomplete external-reliance list, and the posture omission (O5). The persona's statement that it 'had to spend a meaningful share of my session working out which parts of the tool to believe' is the verify-everything anchor. Held at 1 rather than 0 because the persona also reported that every fact in the orientation paragraph it checked held.

unaided_recovery.note: Detected and discounted both garbage lenses, recognised the contamination pattern and discounted it, resolved the Keychain contradiction from the tool's own symbol view, and worked around name-only search by guessing which doc comments would carry URLs. Not 4 because it built its leading bug hypothesis on the tour's FallbackLLMService narrative, which describes dead code (O7), and because it attributed the contamination to the analyzer indexing its own output when the directory belongs to the subject (O9).

advertised_paths.evidence: FINDINGS.md section 6; orchestrator probe5.mjs and probe6.mjs
advertised_paths.note: Escape does not close the trust drawer, verified (O13); the persona's 'no visible close control' is REFUTED, TrustDrawer renders a Close button top right. Structure lens at System and Domain levels: see REVIEW for the probe result. Source excerpts truncating with no full-file view is a product limit rather than a failed feature; recorded as the persona's top blocker and carried into the findings. Name-only search: the box is labelled 'Search everything', so the expectation was reasonable; recorded. EXCLUDED: clicking an off-screen graph node fails for an automation driver and pans for a person (rule 8); the two load-time 404s are by design for this bundle; the guided-paths chip did open the modal, which the persona itself records as its own error.

battery.note: No port for the backend (key: 8766), and HTTPS assumed where the key has plain HTTP. The projection carries no port or protocol on any edge (O11).

Step 2 rests on FallbackLLMService, never constructed by the app. Steps 1, 3, 4, 5 and the telemetry step are sound, and the cached-home-LAN-server hypothesis in step 5 is a genuine contribution the key did not anticipate.
Package count 7 is the vestigial Package.swift figure; the tool induced it.
Shape correct; blanks honest; the backend named as the blank that matters.
